scope: One unmodified ordinary-daemon snapshot/quota crash window on a healthy owned L1 filesystem: ordinary quota clear has returned but durable owner/pin/capacity release is blocked by the exact catalog lock. Not arbitrary quota syscall error injection or a latency/SLO test under that lock.
barrier_evidence: Before action the direct daemon child has zero FDs to the stable private catalog lock inode. L1 PID1 holds that exact lock and observes the daemon opening a distinct FD to the same kernel inode, guarded by immutable process start identity. In the pinned ordinary source registry.releaseContext invokes quota.release, including Q_SYNC/readback, before catalog.withLock opens this FD. Zero quota alone is not used to locate the return boundary. This is FD observation plus source call ordering, not direct quota-syscall tracing.
checkpoint: Two simultaneous real KVM snapshot guests, unprivileged UID, distinct fixed private projects and same pristine template.
Victim is durable RECLAIMING with stop confirmed, destruction not confirmed; exact jail/cgroup gone; quota usage/limits/times empty while original initialized v4 owner bytes remain.
New key returns503 while victim quota is empty, preserving instance capacity/reservation rather than equating zero quota to a free owner.
Keeper real VM/data/execution survives victim clear; exactly the two known shared inode hardlink counts decrease by one. Other names/identity/metadata and independent quota charge remain checked.

After the clear boundary the observer performs quota reads only, no quota sync/set/clear. PID1 retains the exact lock descriptor across the successful control reply until the outer owned-L1 power cut.
cold_before_daemon_recovery: Victim quota is still empty and victim jail/cgroup still absent. Both original durable initialized owner byte strings remain exact.
Keeper immutable hard policy, project/inheritance/namespace accounting and read-only shared snapshot content hashes checked before ordinary recovery.
Catalog active template unchanged, two pins still retained despite victim zero quota and absent private namespace.
recovery: Ordinary daemon recovers both old references to durable DESTROYED; exact old resources/owners gone, both old keys410. Assigned guests are never restored.
Fresh actual KVM/unprivileged guest/new boot/exec/destroy succeeds; all four private project records empty.
Both old pins released; same active pristine catalog template remains with zero pins.
not_claimed: Direct tracing of a Q_SYNC syscall-return event; the return boundary is inferred from the exact observed FD and verified source order.
A new backend allocator reservation while the catalog lock is held; capacity503 and retained durable owner/pins are the observed evidence.
Prepare/switch latency under a deliberately held global catalog lock, percentiles or SLO.
All quota syscall failure/hold/crash windows or physical shared-L0 power/media failure.
